body.x: HADA Co., Ltd. (CEO Jongwoo Ha) participated in the Global Media Meet-Up held on July 1 in collaboration with U.S. tech media outlet Ubergizmo, targeting Korean startups and companies.

Co-hosted by global media outlets AVING News and Ubergizmo, the Global Media Meet-Up aims to introduce domestic technologies and products to the worldwide market. It also serves to promote CES 2026 Innovation Award applicants and startup exhibitors to international media outlets and business partners in a preemptive manner.

HADA, founded in 2012 with the development of a garlic planter, has grown into a specialized agricultural machinery company by mechanizing the entire process of field crop farming. The company has expanded beyond equipment supply to offer comprehensive farming solutions, now leading the advanced agricultural machinery market by integrating smart control systems and agrarian robotics based on autonomous driving technology. With in-house development and production capabilities in both hardware and software, HADA has been delivering practical, field-oriented products and is accelerating global market entry through collaborations with renowned research institutions.

With strong capabilities in developing machinery for all stages of field crop farming and agricultural robotics, HADA has introduced AI and digital transformation (DX) into its operations. It has developed and commercialized unmanned agricultural transport robots, greenhouse sprayers, and orchard sprayers in Korea and is preparing for rapid overseas expansion.

In 2024, HADA launched its flagship product, the unmanned orchard spraying robot ‘Purida P1’, and was recognized by international research institutions as the only Korean company to commercialize such a robot, further validating its technological excellence.

body.cap: Jongwoo Ha, CEO of HADA, delivers a pitch during the Global Media Meet-Up with Ubergizmo held at MIK BaseCamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul on Tuesday, July 1 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The greenhouse spraying robot and follower transport robot developed through smart farming R&D are now entering commercialization. Since 2025, they have been supplied to actual farms through the government’s New Technology Distribution Project, marking a successful application of R&D to real-world use.

HADA also revealed that it was selected for Korea’s national testbed project, which will enable large-scale testing of its unmanned orchard spraying robots starting in the second half of 2025. This initiative is expected to strengthen the robot’s market competitiveness further.

HADA signed an MOU with French agri-tech firm MYDITEK, establishing a foothold in the European market and forming a strategic partnership to expand globally. It has also partnered with Japanese nozzle manufacturer Arimitsu to improve key component technology and product quality through international cooperation.

Based on these domestic and international achievements, HADA is striving to become a leading K-AgriTech company in the global market, enhancing its competitiveness through proven technology and strong partnerships.

The company is preparing to launch its next-generation unmanned orchard spraying robot, ‘Purida P2’, in the first half of next year and aims to submit it for the CES 2026 Innovation Award. ‘Purida P2’ is fully autonomous, designed to address chronic issues in agriculture, including labor shortages, pesticide exposure, and environmental pollution.

The robot utilizes an AI-based terrain learning algorithm that integrates GPS, LiDAR, and vision sensor data in real-time, enabling it to navigate complex orchard layouts in 3D, avoid obstacles, and return automatically to its starting point after completing its task.

body.cap: AI-powered unmanned orchard spraying robot ‘Purida P2’ | Image provided by HADA

body.x: Purida P2 features a high-precision electrostatic nozzle system that attaches pesticide particles evenly to the underside of leaves, reducing pesticide use by 30–40%. A multi-blade system enables individual control of spray strength and direction, making it suitable for various crops, including apples, pears, and grapes. Domestic patents and multiple design rights protect the spray module.

The robot is 100% electrically powered, features a lightweight body that is 49.5% lighter than previous models, and utilizes a high-capacity lithium-ion battery that supports over 5 hours of operation—more than six times longer than drones—making it ideal for large-scale farms. Users can control the robot and manage task data via a cloud-based remote management platform, improving both productivity and sustainability.

In terms of design, Purida P2 embodies a “functional minimalism” philosophy, featuring a sleek, practical form that is well-suited for agricultural use. Its low center of gravity ensures stability on uneven terrain, while its modular structure allows for compatibility with other devices.

The aerodynamic housing, which integrates the electrostatic nozzle and multi-blower, enhances spray efficiency. Sensors are precisely positioned for optimal performance while being protected from external impacts.
The robot’s UX/UI has also been enhanced, featuring an intuitive 7-inch touchscreen and a smartphone-compatible remote control app that enables users to monitor and manage operations easily.

By integrating cutting-edge technologies, Purida P2 contributes to solving major global challenges. In terms of food security, it reduces crop loss from pests and ensures stable food production. It supports health security by eliminating pesticide exposure and reducing the burden of heavy labor for farmers.

The robot also contributes to environmental security by reducing pesticide use and carbon emissions, and to economic and community security by lowering labor and pesticide costs, increasing farm income, and promoting rural sustainability.

body.cap: AI-powered unmanned orchard spraying robot ‘Purida P2’ in action | Image provided by HADA

body.x: At the meet-up, HADA revealed that it is targeting key markets including North America (centered on the U.S.), the EU (focused on France and Germany), and Asia (including Japan). To facilitate this, the company plans to participate in international trade shows, such as CES, to connect with local testing partners and buyers. It is also working to obtain CE and FCC certifications to meet international technical standards and establish a bridgehead for overseas expansion.

As a certified research-based company, HADA also shared its long-term roadmap for transforming the future of agriculture. Under the leadership of CEO Jongwoo Ha, the company aims to build a sustainable agricultural ecosystem by advancing robot technology and expanding into eco-friendly agrarian platforms.

HADA plans to systematically expand its product portfolio to achieve full automation of farm operations. In addition to refining greenhouse and orchard spraying robots, it intends to develop high-versatility sprayers for rice paddies and open fields. The company is also preparing to enter the core agricultural machinery market with future developments in tractors.

Furthermore, HADA is conducting ongoing R&D for fruit thinning and harvesting robots, one of the ultimate goals of agricultural automation. This complex field, requiring image recognition and robotic arm grippers, is expected to take 3–5 years of additional research to achieve complete harvesting automation.

body.cap: HADA CEO Jongwoo Ha (left) and Ubergizmo CTO Hubert Nguyen hold a Q&A session during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK BaseCamp on July 1 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: HADA emphasized that “safety” is the most important value in all its robot and machine development. The company plans to continue investing in safety technologies to prevent harm in unmanned environments.

Finally, CEO Jongwoo Ha shared his long-term vision for the company and its products. “We expect agricultural robot sales to reach break-even in about five years and become a major growth engine for the company. This will allow us to recruit more talent and expand our R&D centers and manufacturing facilities,” he said.

“The ultimate goal of HADA is not just to sell robots, but to help farmers cultivate with greater happiness. By reducing physical labor through technology, we aim to enable farmers to work with pride in a healthier environment. Based on this philosophy, our long-term vision is to become a globally recognized agricultural robotics company within the next 10 to 20 years.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo operates the Silicon Valley Post and publishes in six languages across 200 countries. It focuses on electronics and tech coverage, regularly reporting from major global exhibitions, including CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen, who previously worked as a programmer at NVIDIA and in 3D graphics, attended the event and has covered CES for years.
